title: 45 tok/s Qwen3.8-27B MTP3 on modded RTX 2080 Ti 22GB with my NInfer port
author: xrailgun
post_body:
Repost
Go to LocalLLaMA

1d ago
xrailgun
45 tok/s Qwen3.8-27B MTP3 on modded RTX 2080 Ti 22GB with my NInfer port
Discussion

NInfer is a from-scratch C++/CUDA inference engine that was originally written around RTX 5090 / Blackwell. We ported and tuned it for NVIDIA Turing (sm_75), specifically targeting the 22GB modded RTX 2080 Ti. (NOT COMPATIBLE with unmodded 11GB cards)

TLDR

Using the official groupwise-int (W8A16) artifact and Q8 KV:

Standard Autoregressive (MTP0): ~25 tok/s

Speculative Decode (MTP3, draft window = 3): ~456 tok/s (~65% acceptance rate)

VRAM Usage: ~17.5 GiB total with MTP draft weights loaded, leaving ~4.5–5.0 GiB free for KV cache (allows ~128k context with Q8 KV).

As with the original project, this still includes OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible HTTP serving (/v1/chat/completions, streaming, function calling) and a standalone CLI.

Repo & build instructions: https://github.com/mr-september/ninfer-2080ti-22g

Let me know if you run into any issues building or running it on your setup!

Share

No idea, I doubt it'd be better than UD3.0. However generating ".ninfer" artifacts seem to be open-source so if you're interested in running fine-tunes or uncensored/abliterated versions, this might be a benefit. UD2.0/3.0's exact recipe/code is proprietary.

SarcasticBaka
•
1d ago

Alright I'm giving this a try and have a few questions if you don't mind.

I'm serving using 3.8-27b using the following command: ./build/apps/ninfer-serve models/qwen3_8_27b.ninfer
--host 0.0.0.0
--port 8080
--max-context 16384
--kv-dtype int8
--kv-capacity auto
--max-concurrency 1
--spec mtp --draft-tokens 3 --lm-head-draft

But it only seems to allocate 16k tokens of kv-cache and consumes about 18.2 GBs of VRAM, I thought "--kv-capacity auto" would automatically fill up all the remaining VRAM but perhaps I should be manually setting up max_context to 128k?

After launching the server, testing the curl request gives me the following error:
[2026-08-21 11:51:20.245] [info] ninfer-serve: [req 1] rejected phase=prepare protocol=openai_chat_completions non-stream msgs=2 media=0 tools=0 status=503 code=service_unavailable message=inference engine is unavailable

xrailgun
•
1d ago
•
Edited 1d ago

KV Cache Size: --kv-capacity auto is bounded by max_concurrency * max_context. With --max-concurrency 1 and --max-context 16384, kv capacity maxes out at 16384. If you want to use the remaining ~3.5-4 GB of VRAM for a longer context window, increase --max-context (e.g. --max-context 32768 or 65536), or bump --max-concurrency.

503 / Engine Unavailable: The background worker crashed during warmup on startup.

Please git pull the latest commit: the server will now fail fast on startup and print the exact exception directly.

You can also test with the CLI to isolate the failing kernel/step: ./build/apps/ninfer models/qwen3_8_27b.ninfer -p "hi" --max-context 16384 --kv-dtype int8

If CUDA Graph capture or MTP kernels fail on Turing/SM75, try running with --no-cuda-graph or dropping --spec mtp to isolate which SM75 path failed.

SarcasticBaka
•
1d ago

Alright setting max-context to 65536 with max-concurrency 2 results in 20.8 Gbs of VRAM usage with the server showing [info] ninfer-serve: KV capacity auto resolved=80704, so not exactly the expected 128k context.

pulling the latest commit and testing the cli results in this gibberish: sese掅 Maggioastreiganollapse攱道人ura submajorat橢햨읥擇eday蜊麽띰quals meb Públ Sehatmateratọ쳱띪穫 error: invalid UTF-8 leading byte in generated token stream

xrailgun
•
4h ago

Thanks for testing and reporting this! I reproduced and just pushed fixes to master. Here is a breakdown:

KV Capacity (resolved=80704) This is actually working as expected on a 22 GB card:

The 27B model weights take ~17.2 GB, plus ~1.5 GB for CUDA runtime, activations, and scratch buffers, leaving ~2.6 GB free VRAM.

With --kv-dtype int8, each token requires ~32 KB across all attention layers.

2.6 GB ÷ 32 KB ≈ 80,704 tokens. --kv-capacity auto dynamically fills all remaining physical VRAM on your GPU, which genuinely caps at ~80k tokens on a 22 GB card. To geniunely reach ~128k tokens we'd need to either go down in model quant or KV quant, neither are really great IMO.

2. Gibberish Generation (Fixed)

The invalid UTF-8 / gibberish output was caused by a coordinate unpacking mismatch and dynamic range clipping in the Turing SM75 Gated Delta Net (GDN) chunked prefill kernel.

The SM75 MMA emulation path has been rewritten with exact FP32 SIMT shuffles and verified.

Please pull the latest commit, rebuild:

git pull
ninja -C build

and let me know if this is still happening.
